name: Chronic myelogenous leukemia

meta.title: CML in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults; chronic-phase frontline (TKI selection by comorbidity), milestone monitoring, treatment-free-remission attempts, resistance routing, and advanced-phase disease. WHO-HAEM5 reclassified CML as biphasic (no accelerated phase); ICC retains AP - the divergence is a named teaching point.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for CML - oncology's normal-life-expectancy disease, where the decisions are about HOW to live with (or without) a daily pill: which TKI fits this patient's comorbidities (cardiovascular history gates nilotinib/ponatinib, pleural risk gates dasatinib), whether the IS-qPCR milestones are being met, whether a deep responder should attempt treatment-free remission (EURO-SKI: half succeed, and relapsers regain response on restart), and how resistance mutations route the next line (T315I owns asciminib/ponatinib). The monitoring device IS the disease's core tec…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022, biphasic) / ICC 2022 (retains accelerated phase); ELTS risk score at diagnosis
meta.response: BCR::ABL1 International Scale (IS) qPCR: ELN milestones at 3/6/12 months; MMR (MR3, <=0.1% IS); DMR (MR4/MR4.5) for TFR eligibility

stages.label: Diagnosis & risk
stages.question: BCR::ABL1 confirmed - and what phase, what ELTS risk?
stages.decision: Confirm the fusion; assign phase (WHO-HAEM5 biphasic vs ICC AP - say which) and ELTS score.

stages.label: Comorbidity fit
stages.question: Which TKI fits THIS body?
stages.decision: Cardiovascular history gates nilotinib (and ponatinib later); pleural/pulmonary risk gates dasatinib; the fit question outranks the potency question.

stages.label: Frontline TKI
stages.question: Generic imatinib, a second-generation TKI, or asciminib - for what goal?
stages.decision: Rank the frontline menu; molecular-response surrogates display with labels.

stages.label: Milestone monitoring
stages.question: Is the IS-qPCR on track at 3/6/12 months?
stages.decision: ELN milestones drive the switch conversation; >10% IS at 3 months is failure when confirmed.

stages.label: Advanced phase & transplant
stages.question: When does the transplant conversation return?
stages.decision: Advanced-phase disease and multi-TKI failure reopen allogeneic transplant.

stages.label: Resistance / intolerance
stages.question: Which mutation, how many prior TKIs - and what does that route?
stages.decision: T315I owns asciminib/ponatinib; multi-TKI failure earned ASCEMBL's randomized answer; intolerance is not resistance.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which studies fit - TFR optimization or resistance?

stages.label: Data artifacts
stages.question: Which result moves the plan most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live VOI flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A modifier only - near-normal life expectancy is the norm across ages in chronic phase (ELN 2025).
Patient.helpPatient: In this disease, age changes side-effect planning more than survival.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Modifier only; chronic-phase CML rarely limits function at diagnosis.
Patient.helpPatient: Most people feel close to normal at diagnosis - and stay that way.

Diagnostic gates.label: BCR::ABL1 confirmation
Diagnostic gates.help: The diagnosis is one fusion gene; ranking waits for it.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: One definitive gene test - everything follows from it.

Diagnostic gates.label: Disease phase
Diagnostic gates.help: WHO-HAEM5 made CML biphasic (chronic/blast); ICC retains an accelerated phase - the card names the divergence. 'Advanced' here covers both AP (ICC) and blast phase.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Most CML is found in the calm chronic phase; advanced phase changes the plan completely.

Comorbidity fit.label: Cardiovascular/arterial history
Comorbidity fit.help: Arterial-occlusive risk gates nilotinib frontline and ponatinib at resistance - the comorbidity-fit rule in action.
Comorbidity fit.helpPatient: Heart and artery history picks WHICH pill, not whether there is one.

Comorbidity fit.label: Pulmonary/pleural risk
Comorbidity fit.help: Pleural-effusion propensity (lung disease, uncontrolled hypertension, age) gates dasatinib.
Comorbidity fit.helpPatient: Lung history steers away from the one pill known for fluid around the lungs.

On treatment.label: ELN milestone status (IS-qPCR)
On treatment.help: ELN 2020 milestones (>10% IS at 3 months = failure when confirmed); ELN 2025 individualizes the response - dose adjustment before drug abandonment where appropriate.
On treatment.helpPatient: The quarterly blood test that tells us the pill is doing its one job.

On treatment.label: Kinase-domain mutation
On treatment.help: Tested at failure, not routinely. T315I invalidates every classic TKI - asciminib (higher dose) and ponatinib own that space.
On treatment.helpPatient: If the pill stops working, this test explains why and picks the next one.

On treatment.label: Deep molecular response (MR4+) duration
On treatment.help: EURO-SKI eligibility: >=3 years on TKI with >=1 year of sustained deep response - the gate on the treatment-free-remission attempt. Longer DMR duration predicts success.
On treatment.helpPatient: The doorway to trying life without the pill: a deep response held for at least a year.

On treatment.label: Prior TKI count
On treatment.help: After >=2 TKIs, ASCEMBL's randomized comparison applies (asciminib vs bosutinib).
On treatment.helpPatient: How many pills have been tried shapes what is proven next.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Imatinib (generic) - the cost-effective backbone
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: edema, cramps, GI upset - two decades of familiarity
Newly diagnosed.patient: The original targeted pill - two decades of follow-up, generic pricing, and a near-normal life expectancy.

Newly diagnosed.name: Second-generation TKI (dasatinib / nilotinib / bosutinib)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ELN 2025 first-line options; choice by comorbidity fit and TFR ambition
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: agent-specific: pleural effusions (dasatinib), arterial events + QT (nilotinib), GI (bosutinib)
Newly diagnosed.patient: The faster-acting second wave - chosen by which side-effect profile your body can best ignore.

Newly diagnosed.name: Asciminib frontline (STAMP inhibitor)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: newest frontline option (ASC4FIRST basis); label scope - confirm
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: notably fewer discontinuations than comparators in-trial
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest pill, aimed at a different pocket of the same target - deeper responses faster, with survival data still maturing (the card says so).

Newly diagnosed.name: Treatment-free remission attempt (eligible deep responders)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ELN 2025: TFR is a standard goal for eligible patients
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a withdrawal syndrome (musculoskeletal) in a minority; the real cost is monitoring intensity
Newly diagnosed.patient: For deep responders: stopping the pill entirely, with a tight testing net. Half stay in remission; the other half restart and regain response - nobody in the trial lost ground permanently.

Newly diagnosed.name: Advanced-phase therapy (TKI intensification -> transplant evaluation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ELN 2025: transplant remains valuable when long-term control is not achieved; access broadened
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the rare aggressive form: the pills become the bridge, and transplant becomes the destination.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.patient: Even declining the pill leaves years - stated honestly beside a near-normal-lifespan alternative that costs one tablet a day.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Switch TKI (mutation-guided, non-T315I)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: ELN 2025 sequencing; mutation report picks the agent
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The next pill, chosen by the resistance test rather than by guesswork.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Asciminib (>=2 prior TKIs; T315I at higher dose)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: ELN 2025 option post >=2 TKIs; the randomized answer in that space
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The different-pocket pill, with the only randomized win in the after-two-pills situation.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Ponatinib (T315I; multi-resistant)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: ELN 2025: T315I territory (with asciminib); dose-optimize per OPTIC
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: arterial occlusive events - the gate exists for a reason
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The pill that covers the hardest mutation - with an artery-risk trade the gate takes seriously.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Allogeneic transplant (advanced phase / multi-TKI failure)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: treatment-related mortality and GVHD - disclosed verbatim beside benefit per honesty constraint
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The one-time cure held in reserve for when the pills cannot hold the line.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort first, always on the menu.

milestones.title: Molecular milestones on the clock
review: the ELN molecular clock IS the disease management: >10% BCR::ABL1 at 3 months (confirmed) = failure (ELN-2020 verbatim); ELN-2025 individualizes the switch response
ELTS risk score at diagnosis (not Sokal) per ELN-2020
the TFR goal reframes 1L choice: deep-molecular-response speed matters if stopping is the ambition (EURO-SKI: longer DMR duration predicts success OR 1.13/year)
adherence check BEFORE resistance work-up at every rising transcript

FERTILITY PRESERVATION (the precondition law): Oktay et al., 'Fertility Preservation in Patients With Cancer: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update' (J Clin Oncol 2018;36:1994-2001 - PMID 29620997, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): initiate the infertility discussion AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE in patients treated during reproductive years (or parents/guardians of children); refer candidates to reproductive specialists; DOCUMENT the discussion. Sperm, oocyte, and embryo cryopreservation are standard practice; GnRHa is not a substitute for proven methods.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' is in the manifest staleness list.
Molecular-response surrogates (MMR at 24/48 weeks) display with labels and NEVER rank against survival - ASC4FIRST's superiority is a surrogate superiority and the card says so.
The TFR card states both halves: half stay in remission, half restart and regain response - and that EURO-SKI's safety depended on the monthly monitoring net.
ELN 2025's individualization renders verbatim on the warning branch: adherence and dose review before drug abandonment.
The WHO-HAEM5 / ICC phase divergence is named on the phase input, not silently resolved.
Ponatinib's arterial-occlusive gate applies exactly when the drug is most tempting (T315I) - the gate renders with that sentence.
Transplant cards disclose TRM beside benefit; transplant renders only for advanced phase / multi-TKI failure.
The trial entry is an explicit unverified placeholder and renders as needs-verification.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: BCR::ABL1 must be confirmed before ranking
advanced-phase disease reroutes to the intensive + transplant pathway
arterial-occlusive risk gates nilotinib (frontline) and ponatinib (resistance)
care: Structured TFR monitoring program (monthly qPCR turnaround)

surveillance.cadence: IS-qPCR quarterly on treatment; monthly for 6 months after a TFR attempt, then every 2 months (EURO-SKI-style)
